problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign packages to identical delivery trucks.  
Packages:  
* Package Alpha: volume 41 cubic feet  
* Package Beta: volume 58 cubic feet  
* Package Gamma: volume 44 cubic feet  
* Package Delta: volume 32 cubic feet  
* Package Epsilon: volume 35 cubic feet  
* Package Zeta: volume 44 cubic feet  
* Package Eta: volume 55 cubic feet  
* Package Theta: volume 55 cubic feet  
* Package Iota: volume 57 cubic feet  
* Package Kappa: volume 70 cubic feet  
* Package Lambda: volume 31 cubic feet  
* Package Mu: volume 39 cubic feet  
* Package Nu: volume 69 cubic feet  
* Package Xi: volume 48 cubic feet  
* Package Omicron: volume 49 cubic feet  
* Package Pi: volume 32 cubic feet  
* Package Rho: volume 66 cubic feet  
* Package Sigma: volume 43 cubic feet  
* Package Tau: volume 49 cubic feet  
* Package Upsilon: volume 61 cubic feet  
* Package Phi: volume 54 cubic feet  
* Package Chi: volume 37 cubic feet  
* Package Psi: volume 69 cubic feet  
* Package Omega: volume 52 cubic feet  
* Package A1: volume 35 cubic feet  
* Package B1: volume 59 cubic feet  
* Package C1: volume 53 cubic feet  
* Package D1: volume 44 cubic feet  
* Package E1: volume 69 cubic feet  
* Package F1: volume 67 cubic feet  
* Package G1: volume 32 cubic feet  
* Package H1: volume 36 cubic feet  
* Package I1: volume 52 cubic feet  
* Package J1: volume 59 cubic feet  
* Package K1: volume 42 cubic feet  

Each truck can carry up to 100 cubic feet of volume. Assign all packages using the fewest trucks. Each package must be placed in exactly one truck, and the total volume in a truck cannot exceed its capacity.
